Solves the lack of a standard non-electronic (paper) backup format that other wallets already offer
Aimed at users who want a human-writable, error-correcting backup instead of a digital-only one

result.summary: This POC adds codex32-based paper backups to the Bitcoin Core wallet: a ported codex32 encoder/decoder, a new wallet flag and on-disk storage for the raw HD seed, and two new RPCs (exposesecret to export the seed as codex32, recoverwalletfromseed to rebuild a wallet from it), plus unit and functional tests. It touches wallet creation call sites throughout the codebase to thread an optional seed key through CreateWallet and SetupDescriptorScriptPubKeyMans.
result.problem: Bitcoin Core currently has no standard human-writable (non-electronic) backup format; other wallets in the ecosystem have offered codex32-style paper backups for years, and users who want an offline, error-correcting backup have no first-class option. The author explicitly frames this as a proposal to gauge whether the feature and this particular approach are wanted.

open_concerns: Sjors: this may duplicate the addhdkey/gethdkeys direction being pursued in #32652 and should be discussed as part of a broader design for paper backups covering keys, descriptors, and metadata separately.

BenWestgate: the design lacks passphrase/threshold handling matching BIP-93, lacks timestamp support needed to recover existing wallets safely, and should support codex32 shares (not just full secrets).
rkrux: has not reviewed code yet but flags that a timestamp is likely needed and that other approaches tie import/restore to a corresponding descriptor for robustness.
resolved_concerns: apoelstra's point that the wallet passphrase adds no security once the seed is exposed was acknowledged by the author as correct.

result.card: This draft POC adds codex32 paper-backup support to the Bitcoin Core wallet: it stores the raw HD seed on disk behind a new wallet flag and adds exposesecret/recoverwalletfromseed RPCs to export and restore it in a human-writable, error-correcting format. The problem is real: reviewer rkrux calls paper backup 'highly desirable' given it is standard elsewhere, but the design is contested, with Sjors suggesting the approach duplicates the addhdkey/gethdkeys path in #32652 and BenWestgate flagging missing timestamp and share-based recovery support. The author has been silent since July 2025 despite a year of intermittent concept discussion, so the PR is stale and any code review risks being invalidated by a rework. It conflicts with several other open wallet PRs touching the same files (achow101's wallet-version and transaction-storage work, roconnor-blockstream's addhdkey codex32 PR). No formal dependency is declared, but it is conceptually entangled with #32652 and the broader paper-backup design discussion Sjors proposed opening as a separate issue.
